title: Comparing a Portfolio of Stocks
text: comparing stocks vastly different share prices (e.g., $150 vs. $3,000), plotting raw prices chart isn’t helpful. Instead, can normalize prices. common approach set price start date 100 stocks, allowing intuitive like--like comparison percentage growth. can accomplish effortlessly using dplyr grouping data symbol dividing every daily closing price first closing price group. ’ll also convert POSIXct datetime standard Date object cleaner plotting later. (example, normalized value 118 indicates 18% growth initial investment date.)
code: portfolio_performance <- portfolio_prices |>   # Group calculations by ticker and ensure chronological sorting within group   group_by(symbol) |>   arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) |>   mutate(     # Convert to Date to drop intraday timezone info for cleaner plotting     date = as.Date(date),     # Normalize price to 100 on the first day     normalized_price = (close / close[1]) * 100   ) |>   ungroup()  # View the latest normalized performance portfolio_performance |>   group_by(symbol) |>   slice_tail(n = 1) |>   select(symbol, date, close, normalized_price) #> # A tibble: 4 × 4 #>   symbol date       close normalized_price #>   <chr>  <date>     <dbl>            <dbl> #> 1 AAPL   2024-08-21  225.             118. #> 2 AMZN   2024-08-21  182.             135. #> 3 GOOGL  2024-08-21  163.             122. #> 4 MSFT   2024-08-21  421.             128.

title: Event Study: Earnings Announcements and Price Reactions
text: guide, run miniature event study: measure stock reacts earnings announcements, stripping market’s general drift. workflow standard one event-study literature, simplified market-adjusted model: Pick announcement dates (events). Download price history stock benchmark index around date. Compute daily returns; abnormal return (ARtAR_t) stock’s return minus benchmark’s return day. Accumulate ARtAR_t across event window (, 2 days 5 days announcement) obtain cumulative abnormal return (CAR). (Note: full event study estimate stock-specific beta pre-event estimation window test CARs statistical significance. market-adjusted shortcut shown assumes beta ≈ 1—fine exploration visualization, treat inference care.)

title: Event Study: Earnings Announcements and Price Reactions
text: helper pivots window one row per day side--side price columns, computes daily returns series, aligns every row announcement day (rel_day 0), keeps event window: Running single event shows shape result—announcement reaction lands rel_day 0 1 depending whether release came bell:
code: compute_ar <- function(label, event_date) {   raw <- yf_download_prices(     tickers  = c("AAPL", "^GSPC"),     start    = event_date - 14,     end      = event_date + 14,     interval = "1d"   )    raw |>     mutate(symbol = if_else(symbol == "^GSPC", "index", symbol)) |>     select(date, symbol, close) |>     pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = close) |>     arrange(date) |>     mutate(       ret_stock = AAPL / lag(AAPL) - 1,       ret_mkt   = index / lag(index) - 1,       ar        = ret_stock - ret_mkt     ) |>     # Locate the first session on/after the announcement (t = 0)     mutate(rel_day = row_number() - which(as.Date(date) >= event_date)[1]) |>     filter(rel_day %in% -2:5) |>     transmute(label, rel_day, ar) } ar_q1 <- compute_ar("FY26 Q1", as.Date("2026-01-29"))  ar_q1 #> # A tibble: 8 x 3 #>   label   rel_day       ar #>   <chr>      <int>    <dbl> #> 1 FY26 Q1       -2 -0.0042 #> 2 FY26 Q1       -1  0.0019 #> 3 FY26 Q1        0  0.0031 #> 4 FY26 Q1        1  0.0384 #> 5 FY26 Q1        2  0.0057 #> # i 3 more rows

text: Now run helper every event map2_dfr() accumulate: thin lines show announcement’s CAR path, thick line average: (Note: arrange(rel_day, .by_group = TRUE) sorts within event running sum never crosses event boundaries; replace_na() guards leading NA return.)
code: car_paths <- map2_dfr(events$label, events$event_date, compute_ar) |>   group_by(label) |>   arrange(rel_day, .by_group = TRUE) |>   mutate(car = cumsum(replace_na(ar, 0))) |>   ungroup()  avg_car <- car_paths |>   group_by(rel_day) |>   summarise(car = mean(car), .groups = "drop") ggplot() +   geom_line(data = car_paths,             aes(x = rel_day, y = car, group = label),             color = "#9aa5ad", linewidth = 0.5) +   geom_line(data = avg_car, aes(x = rel_day, y = car),             color = "#1f77b4", linewidth = 1.2) +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#555555") +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = -2:5) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +   labs(     title    = "Average Cumulative Abnormal Return — AAPL Earnings",     subtitle = "Grey: individual announcements; blue: average",     x        = "Trading days relative to announcement",     y        = "Cumulative abnormal return",     caption  = "Source: Yahoo Finance via yahoofinancer"   ) +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

Caveats: single-stock CARs conflate firm news sector news (S&P 500 imperfect control); without significance testing, treat magnitudes descriptive . cookbook’s rolling-correlation recipe (vignette("cookbook", package = "yahoofinancer")) natural next step toward proper factor controls.

text: complete, self-contained workflow single copy-pasteable script:
code: library(yahoofinancer) library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(purrr) library(ggplot2) library(scales)  # 1. Events: three earnings announcements, two weeks of slack each side events <- tibble::tribble(   ~label,    ~event_date,   "FY25 Q4", as.Date("2025-10-30"),   "FY26 Q1", as.Date("2026-01-29"),   "FY26 Q2", as.Date("2026-04-30") )  # 2. Market-adjusted abnormal returns over [-2, +5] compute_ar <- function(label, event_date) {   yf_download_prices(c("AAPL", "^GSPC"),                      start = event_date - 14,                      end   = event_date + 14) |>     mutate(symbol = if_else(symbol == "^GSPC", "index", symbol)) |>     select(date, symbol, close) |>     pivot_wider(names_from = symbol, values_from = close) |>     arrange(date) |>     mutate(ret_stock = AAPL / lag(AAPL) - 1,            ret_mkt   = index / lag(index) - 1,            ar        = ret_stock - ret_mkt) |>     mutate(rel_day = row_number() - which(as.Date(date) >= event_date)[1]) |>     filter(rel_day %in% -2:5) |>     transmute(label, rel_day, ar) }  # 3. Cumulate per event and average across events avg_car <- map2_dfr(events$label, events$event_date, compute_ar) |>   group_by(label) |>   arrange(rel_day, .by_group = TRUE) |>   mutate(car = cumsum(replace_na(ar, 0))) |>   ungroup() |>   group_by(rel_day) |>   summarise(car = mean(car), .groups = "drop")  # 4. Plot the average CAR path ggplot(avg_car, aes(x = rel_day, y = car)) +   geom_line(color = "#1f77b4", linewidth = 1.2) +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#555555") +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = -2:5) +   scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +   labs(title = "Average CAR — AAPL Earnings Announcements",        x = "Trading days relative to announcement",        y = "Cumulative abnormal return") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

code: library(yahoofinancer) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(scales)  # 1. Define peer universe tickers <- c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOG")  # 2. Fetch income statement and cash flow statements income_df   <- yf_get_financials(tickers, statement_type = "income", frequency = "annual") cashflow_df <- yf_get_financials(tickers, statement_type = "cash-flow", frequency = "annual")  # 3. Retrieve quarterly valuation measures stocks       <- Tickers$new(tickers) val_measures <- stocks$valuation_measures  # 4. Join and calculate key metrics latest_income <- income_df |>   group_by(symbol) |>   slice_tail(n = 1) |>   ungroup() |>   mutate(operating_margin = operating_income / total_revenue) |>   select(symbol, date, total_revenue, operating_margin)  latest_cf <- cashflow_df |>   group_by(symbol) |>   slice_tail(n = 1) |>   ungroup() |>   mutate(fcf_conversion = free_cash_flow / operating_cash_flow) |>   select(symbol, fcf_conversion)  latest_val <- val_measures |>   group_by(symbol) |>   slice_tail(n = 1) |>   ungroup() |>   select(symbol, pe_ratio, forward_pe_ratio, peg_ratio, enterprise_value_ebitda_ratio)  screener_summary <- latest_income |>   left_join(latest_cf, by = "symbol") |>   left_join(latest_val, by = "symbol")  # 5. Display screener table print(screener_summary)

title: Building a Live Market Dashboard with Shiny
text: cards read stats() reactive. price_card, range_card, volume_card use renderText(), change_card uses renderUI() color percentage move green red based direction. range card places current price within 52-week band. Two defensive details worth keeping: req(stats()) silently suspends rendering first successful fetch—errors flash data arrives. percentage uses scales::percent() explicit accuracy, values like 12.34567% never leak UI.
code: output$price_card <- renderText({     req(stats())     sprintf("%s · %s", stats()$symbol, dollar(stats()$regular_market_price))   })    output$change_card <- renderUI({     s <- req(stats())     pct <- 100 * (s$regular_market_price - s$previous_close) / s$previous_close     color <- if (pct >= 0) "#2e7d32" else "#c62828"     tags$span(style = sprintf("color:%s", color),               sprintf("%+.2f%% vs previous close", pct))   })    output$range_card <- renderText({     s <- req(stats())     pos <- 100 * (s$regular_market_price - s$fifty_two_week_low) /       (s$fifty_two_week_high - s$fifty_two_week_low)     sprintf(       "%s — %s\n(%s of 52-week range)",       dollar(s$fifty_two_week_low), dollar(s$fifty_two_week_high),       percent(pos / 100, accuracy = 1)     )   })    output$volume_card <- renderText({     s <- req(stats())     label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())(s$regular_market_volume)   })

s$previous_close) / s$previous_close     color <- if (pct >= 0) "#2e7d32" else "#c62828"     tags$span(style = sprintf("color:%s", color),               sprintf("%+.2f%% vs previous close", pct))   })   output$range_card <- renderText({     s <- req(stats())     pos <- 100 * (s$regular_market_price - s$fifty_two_week_low) /       (s$fifty_two_week_high - s$fifty_two_week_low)     sprintf("%s — %s\n(%s of range)",             dollar(s$fifty_two_week_low),             dollar(s$fifty_two_week_high),             percent(pos / 100, accuracy = 1))   })   output$volume_card <- renderText({     req(stats())$regular_market_volume |> label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())   })    output$price_chart <- renderPlot({     df <- req(prices())     s  <- req(stats())     ggplot(df, aes(x = date, y = close)) +       geom_line(color = "#1f77b4", linewidth = 0.9) +       geom_hline(yintercept = s$fifty_two_week_high,                  linetype = "dashed", color = "#2e7d32") +       geom_hline(yintercept = s$fifty_two_week_low,                  linetype = "dashed", color = "#c62828") +       scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +       labs(title = paste(s$symbol, "Price History"), x = NULL, y = "Price (USD)") +       theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +       theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: yahoofinancer 0.6.1
text: Financial Statements Restoration: Added working $get_income_statement(), $get_balance_sheet(), $get_cash_flow() methods Ticker backed Yahoo’s fundamentals-timeseries endpoint support frequency = c("annual", "quarterly"). Updated yf_get_financials() return tidy tibbles line items. (#48) Unified HTTP Request Engine: Centralized API communication unified internal api_request() helper automatic retry, timeout, user agent header, structured error reporting across endpoints. (#49) Standardized Failure Contracts: Multi-symbol routines (Tickers$aggregate_data(), yf_download_prices(), yf_get_financials(), yf_get_market_stats(), yf_get_index_quotes()) consistently warn failed symbols return empty tibbles matching documented schemas full failure. (#50) Batch Symbol Validation & Metadata Caching: validate() vectorizes symbol queries single HTTP request. Ticker caches instance metadata, invalidating set_symbol(). (#51) Date Hygiene & Lookback Limit Enforcement: get_history() validates dates client-side enforces intraday lookback boundaries (1m <= 7d, 5m/15m/30m <= 60d, 1h <= 730d). currency_converter() guards NA date inputs. (#52) Hermetic Testing & Fixtures: Redacted httptest2 fixtures financial statements sanitized test mock surfaces. (#53) Package Hygiene: Declared R (>= 4.1) floor, configured .lintr, updated User-Agent include package version. (#54)
